definition: A hyperparameter controlling how much model weights are adjusted with each update during optimization.
details: Too high a learning rate can cause training to diverge or oscillate; too low can make training painfully slow or get stuck in poor local minima. Learning rate schedules (warmup, decay) are widely used to stabilize training.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Learning Rate.
